title: execution-history
description: The coordinator's structured rendering of a run's events, one entry per line appended to events.log, in the same order. History is evidence, never state: no routing decision reads it. The coordinator writes it and does not validate its own write at run time; conformance is checked by the story's tests.

items.description: One event. sequence, timestamp, event and message are present on every entry; the remaining fields appear only on the events that have them.

sequence.description: 1-based position in the stream, matching the line number in events.log.

timestamp.description: Wall-clock time the event was appended, in the same YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS form events.log uses.

event.description: What kind of event this is.

message.description: The prose line as it was written to events.log, without the timestamp prefix.

stage.description: The workflow stage the event belongs to. Absent on events that belong to the run rather than a stage.

artifacts.description: The artifacts the stage produced, taken from that stage's declared outputs in the workflow definition.

duration_seconds.description: Elapsed seconds since the stage started, on the event that ends a stage.

verifier_outcome.description: The verifier's verdict, on events that carry one.

retry_decision.description: The routing decision taken after a failed verification.

retry_reason.description: Why that retry decision was taken.

retry_category.description: The retry category the verifier reported, as the workflow's retry_routing table declares it. Absent on a retry that carries no category, such as a clean-clone failure, and on events that route nothing.

retry_stage.description: The stage the retry was routed to, read off the workflow's declared route rather than a constant. With retry_category it makes the route a reader can reconstruct from the history alone. On a self-routed entry it names the entry's own stage, because a self-route has no destination other than itself; counting the self-routed entries for a stage is therefore a query against this history rather than a number kept anywhere.

findings.description: How many findings an inspection's invocation produced. Absent on every entry that is not an inspection, and present on one that is even where it is zero, because a run whose change had nothing wrong with it is an answer rather than a missing field.

filed.description: How many of those findings reached the outbox as briefs. Absent on every entry that is not an inspection.

dropped.description: How many were dropped, for every reason together: already filed by either dedupe source, already queued, malformed, naming a workflow the harness does not define, past the brief cap, or lost by the queue. Which way each went is in the entry's own message, where each reason is named with how many went that way. Absent on every entry that is not an inspection.

mode.description: Which inspection this entry records: the narrow one a completed run makes of what its story changed. Absent on every entry that is not an inspection. The broad mode an l5-inspect invocation runs in appears in the cross-run inspection log and never here, because it is not made by a run and has no run history to appear in.

cost_usd.description: What the inspection's invocation reported spending, in US dollars, exactly as the runner's own result reported it. Carried and never computed: nothing re-derives it by reading an agent log back. Absent where the invocation reported no cost, rather than written as zero, because a zero is what an inspection that genuinely cost nothing would carry and conflating the two corrupts any average taken later. Absent on every entry that is not an inspection.

scope_files.description: How many files the inspection had in scope. What a cost means depends on how much was read, so the two are recorded together. Absent on every entry that is not an inspection.

invocations.description: How many agent invocations the recorded cost covers. Absent on every entry that is not an inspection, and zero on one recording an inspection that was not made.
